card.name: Waiting until the patient is stable
card.fires_on: Words just before an expected 'stable', 'stabilized' or 'discharge', such as 'patient is', 'clinically', 'until hospital'. Seen in instructions on when to start, resume or stop a treatment.

modes.label: Patient state before 'stable'
modes.description: The verb or adverb after 'the patient' that leads into a stability condition for resuming or starting a drug.
modes.example: Resume bexagliflozin tablets when the patient is<< clinically>> stable and has resumed oral intake [see

modes.label: Until hospital discharge
modes.description: The word 'hospital' in duration limits that run until discharge.
modes.example: The usual duration of Enoxaparin Sodium Injection therapy is 8 days or until<< hospital>> discharge.

modes.label: Patient in acute-care narratives
modes.description: The word 'patient' or its verb in acute-care events, ahead of recovery or stabilization.
modes.example: Continuous epinephrine infusion is generally required over several hours or days until the<< patient>>’s hemodynamic status improves.

card.writes: It pushes the model to predict stable, stabilize, stabilization or discharge next.
card.plain: It fires when the text is about to say a patient is stable or ready for discharge.
